settings.title: Settings
settings.autoLockHint: The vault also locks when Windows locks, when the screen turns off and when the computer sleeps.
settings.kitUnknown: No Emergency Kit has been created on this computer yet.
settings.kitNewExplain: A new recovery key replaces the old one. Destroy your old Emergency Kit afterwards.
settings.rotateIntro: Use this if your master password or recovery key may have been exposed. It replaces the key that encrypts your vault.
rotateExplain: Your vault is re-encrypted with a new key and you get a new recovery key (new Emergency Kit).
Your master password stays the same. Change it as well if it may have been exposed.
The old recovery key stops working for the vault from now on.
Older copies of the vault (the backups folder) still open with the old password and recovery key. Delete them if they may be exposed.
settings.closeToTray: Close button hides xPass to the tray
settings.lockOnMinimize: Lock when xPass is minimized or hidden to the tray
settings.rotateExplainHello: Windows Hello is turned off. You can set it up again right after.

password.tooWeak: Choose a stronger password to continue.

setup.title: Create your vault
setup.intro: Choose a master password. It encrypts your vault and is never stored or sent anywhere. If you forget it, only your Emergency Kit can open the vault.

kit.title: Your Emergency Kit
kit.intro: This recovery key opens your vault if you forget the master password. It is shown only now. Print it or save it as a PDF, and keep it offline somewhere safe.
kit.warning: Anyone with this key and your vault file can read your passwords.
kit.confirmIntro: Type groups {{a}} and {{b}} of your recovery key.
kit.confirmMismatch: These groups do not match. Check your Emergency Kit.
kit.printHowTo: If you forget your master password
printSteps: Open xPass and choose “Use recovery key” on the unlock screen.
Type the recovery key above. Dashes, spaces and letter case do not matter.
kit.printKeep: Keep this sheet offline. Do not store it on the same computer or in the same cloud account as your vault.

hello.title: Windows Hello
hello.intro: Unlock xPass with your face, fingerprint or PIN. Your master password keeps working and is still needed for sensitive changes.
hello.stateOn: Windows Hello is on for this vault.
hello.unavailable: Windows Hello is not set up on this PC. Set up a PIN, face or fingerprint in Windows Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options, then come back here.
hello.unavailableEnrolled: Windows Hello is not available on this PC right now. Unlock with your master password; you can turn Windows Hello off here.
hello.turnOnExplain: Enter your master password. Windows Hello then asks you to confirm it is you.
hello.turnOffMessage: You will unlock xPass with your master password only. You can turn Windows Hello on again at any time.
hello.reenrollMessage: The vault key was changed or Windows Hello was reset on this PC, so Windows Hello no longer unlocks this vault.

sync.title: Sync
sync.intro: Keep this vault in sync across your PCs through a file in a private GitHub repository. Only the encrypted vault is uploaded; GitHub never sees your passwords or your master password.
sync.needsToken: Sync is off until a GitHub token is saved. Choose Change and enter a token.
sync.testFirst: Test the connection before saving. The token is stored in Windows Credential Manager and never shown again.
sync.disconnectMessage: The token is deleted from this PC and xPass stops syncing. Your vault on this PC and the copy on GitHub are not changed.

report.missing: Connected. There is no vault at this path yet; the first sync will create it on branch {{branch}}.
report.sameVault: Connected. This vault is already stored at this path.
report.found: Connected. An xPass vault was found at this path.
report.otherVault: A different xPass vault is stored at this path. Choose another path, or another repository.
report.notAVault: This path holds a file that is not an xPass vault. Choose another path.
report.branchMissing: The branch {{branch}} does not exist in this repository.
report.public: This repository is public. The vault is encrypted, but anyone can download it and its full history. A private repository is strongly recommended.
report.publicAck: I understand and want to use this public repository.

guide.title: How to create a GitHub token
steps: Create a private repository on GitHub for the vault (an empty one is fine).
Open GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens, and choose Generate new token.
Repository access: Only select repositories, and pick the vault repository.
Permissions: Contents: Read and write (Metadata: Read-only is added automatically).
Choose an expiration date, generate the token and paste it here. You can replace it here when it expires.
guide.note: Use a token that can only reach this one repository. Do not reuse a token with wider access.
